#### In this vignette, you learn how bridgenorm can normalize every batch toward a goal distribution: the mean of a chosen set of batches.

By default bridgenorm corrects every batch toward one anchor batch. That is not always the target you want. A study may be run in two phases, and the later phase should be put on the scale of the earlier one, so the earlier analysis (gates, clusters, thresholds) still holds. Or one anchor batch may be noisy, and the mean of several batches is a steadier target. CytoNorm offers this through its goal distribution: the mean over batches by default, one goal batch, or goal quantiles from an earlier model.

bridgenorm has the same choices:

- `target = "anchor"` (the default): the goal is the anchor batch.
- `target = "virtual"`: the goal is the equal-weight mean of all batches. In each SOM node, the goal quantile curve is the mean of the batches' curves; for the paired shift, each bridge summary is the mean over batches.
- `target = "virtual", goal_batches = <batches>`: the goal is the equal-weight mean of the given batches only.

The anchor still sets the bridges and the map, and it may lie outside the goal batches. Batches in `goal_batches` that are unbridged, or whose bridge donors differ from the anchor's, are dropped from the goal. No benchmark benefit of a goal over the anchor target is claimed yet; use it when the design asks for it.

## Prepare the bridgenorm normalization step

```{r library}
library(bridgenorm)
```

Six batches come from two studies: study 1 ran batches b1 to b3, study 2 batches b4 to b6. Each batch holds two bridge wells of one reference donor and two study samples. Between the studies the instrument changed, so all study 2 batches read marker M higher, by 0.6 in cell state A and 0.4 in state B. On top of that, each batch shifts and stretches M by a small amount of its own. We want every batch on the scale of study 2, so the goal is the mean of b4, b5 and b6. The anchor is b1, which lies outside the goal.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(2)
batches <- paste0("b", 1:6)
centre <- c(A = 2, B = 1)
lin <- c(A = 1, B = 4)
study_shift <- c(A = 0.6, B = 0.4) # study 2 reads M higher
effect <- lapply(setNames(batches, batches), function(b) {
  in_study2 <- b %in% c("b4", "b5", "b6")
  list(
    shift = in_study2 * study_shift + c(A = rnorm(1, 0, 0.1), B = rnorm(1, 0, 0.1)),
    scale = exp(rnorm(1, 0, 0.1))
  )
})
samples <- data.frame(
  sample_id = c(outer(c("ref1", "ref2", "s1", "s2"), batches, paste, sep = "_")),
  batch = rep(batches, each = 4),
  reference_id = rep(c("donor", "donor", NA, NA), 6),
  aliquot = rep(c("ref1", "ref2", NA, NA), 6)
)
samples$study <- ifelse(samples$batch %in% c("b1", "b2", "b3"), "study1", "study2")
cells <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(samples)), function(i) {
  b <- samples$batch[i]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("A", "B"), function(k) {
    truth <- rnorm(300, centre[[k]], 0.3)
    data.frame(
      sample_id = samples$sample_id[i],
      Lin = rnorm(300, lin[[k]], 0.2),
      M = centre[[k]] + effect[[b]]$scale * (truth - centre[[k]]) + effect[[b]]$shift[[k]]
    )
  }))
}))
cells$batch <- samples$batch[match(cells$sample_id, samples$sample_id)]
is_bridge <- !is.na(samples$reference_id[match(cells$sample_id, samples$sample_id)])
```

The goal batches are all batches of study 2:

```{r goal}
goal <- unique(samples$batch[samples$study == "study2"])
goal
```

## Train the bridgenorm models

One model per goal, so the three targets can be compared: the anchor b1, the mean of all batches, and the mean of study 2.

```{r fit}
fit <- function(...) {
  bn_fit(
    x = cells[, c("sample_id", "Lin", "M")],
    samples = samples,
    population = rep("T", nrow(cells)),
    markers = c("Lin", "M"),
    transform = list(name = "asinh", cofactor = 5),
    anchor = "b1",
    grid = c(2, 1),
    mapping_markers = "Lin",
    seed = 1,
    train_cells = 300,
    rlen = 50,
    ...
  )
}
models <- list(
  anchor = fit(),
  all_batches = fit(target = "virtual"),
  study2 = fit(target = "virtual", goal_batches = goal)
)
models$study2$settings$goal_batches
```

The goal is recorded in the model and covered by its digest, so a saved model says which batches it normalizes toward.

## Apply the bridgenorm models

```{r apply}
corrected <- lapply(models, function(m) {
  bn_apply(m, cells[, c("sample_id", "Lin", "M")], samples, rep("T", nrow(cells)))$x$M
})
```

## Evaluate the quality

### Density plots

The density of M in the bridge cells of each batch (study 1 in reds, study 2 in blues), with the goal distribution in purple: the pooled bridge cells of the goal batches before correction, each batch weighted equally. Toward the anchor, every batch moves to study 1's scale; toward the mean of all batches, every batch lands between the studies; toward the study 2 goal, every batch, study 1 included, moves onto the purple curve.

```{r density, fig.height = 5}
colours <- setNames(c("#900002", "#E66100", "#FFB000", "#0046A1", "#3C9BE6", "#6FCFFF"), batches)
goal_cells <- unlist(lapply(goal, function(b) {
  sample(cells$M[is_bridge & cells$batch == b], 600)
}))
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
panels <- list(uncorrected = cells$M, anchor = corrected$anchor, `all batches` = corrected$all_batches,
  `study 2 goal` = corrected$study2)
for (panel in names(panels)) {
  plot(NULL, xlim = c(-0.5, 4), ylim = c(0, 1.6), xlab = "M", ylab = "Density", main = panel)
  for (b in batches) lines(density(panels[[panel]][is_bridge & cells$batch == b]), col = colours[[b]])
  lines(density(goal_cells), col = "#7209B7", lwd = 2.5)
}
legend("topright", legend = c(batches, "goal"), col = c(colours, "#7209B7"), lwd = c(rep(1, 6), 2.5),
  bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
par(op)
```

### Distance to the goal

The earth mover's distance (EMD) between each batch's corrected bridge cells and the goal distribution; lower means closer to the goal. Only the model with the study 2 goal is meant to bring every batch to it; the other two are shown for contrast. Bridge cells were used to fit the models, so this checks that the goal was reached, not how well the correction generalizes; held-out bridge wells do that (see the [comparison article](compare.html)).

```{r emd}
emd <- function(a, b) mean(abs(quantile(a, ppoints(200)) - quantile(b, ppoints(200))))
to_goal <- sapply(c(list(uncorrected = cells$M), corrected), function(v) {
  sapply(setNames(batches, batches), function(b) emd(v[is_bridge & cells$batch == b], goal_cells))
})
round(to_goal, 3)
```

### Quantile-map plots

In each node, the study 2 model maps every batch's quantiles onto the goal's: the mean of the goal batches' quantile curves, stored under the virtual key. The maps sit close to the diagonal because the tables are on the pass-1 scale: the pass-1 node shift has already moved every batch to the goal's location, and the maps correct what is left of each batch's shape.

```{r quantile-maps}
q <- models$study2$quantiles
key_batch <- sub("\r.*", "", names(q))
key_node <- sub(".*\r", "", names(q))
virtual <- unique(key_batch[!key_batch %in% batches])
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
for (node in unique(key_node)) {
  goal_q <- q[[which(key_batch == virtual & key_node == node)]][, "M"]
  node_q <- unlist(lapply(q[key_node == node], function(x) x[, "M"]))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(node_q), ylim = range(goal_q),
    xlab = "Batch quantiles of M", ylab = "Goal quantiles of M", main = node)
  abline(0, 1, col = "grey70", lty = 2)
  for (b in batches) {
    i <- which(key_batch == b & key_node == node)
    if (length(i) == 1) lines(q[[i]][, "M"], goal_q, col = colours[[b]], type = "b", pch = 20)
  }
}
par(op)
```

## Notes

- A goal set of one batch is the anchor target: use `target = "anchor"` with that batch as anchor.
- When the anchor lies outside the goal, the goal must measure every bridge summary the anchor has (each reference donor, population and marker); otherwise `bn_fit()` stops with a message rather than produce a missing target.
- `bn_fit_paired()` takes the same `target` and `goal_batches` arguments.
- To add later batches to an existing goal without changing earlier corrections, keep the model and apply it ([use case 3](frozen-model.html)).
